o1.biggest_strength: It reads like a production brief. Each concept has timed scenes, a headline with character count, and a sound-honesty note. The three picks follow the data (women's cost per purchase, work flyers, quiet wheels). It also sets a test budget with a clear win and stop rule, and keeps claims strictly to the approved specs.
o1.biggest_mistake: The concept details are uneven, and the "who and awareness" and "tests" fields sit in a table instead of under each concept. Concepts 2 and 7 are both proof-led and feel close. The "lifts it into a cab with one hand" shot hints at lightness beyond the approved spec.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put awareness and test variable under every concept. Swap one proof-led concept for a bolder idea. Drop the one-hand lift. Tighten the primary text into shorter, calmer lines in our voice.

o2.biggest_strength: It follows my requested structure for every concept: angle, who and awareness, hook, format, visual, text, test. The primary text is short and calm in our voice. It reads the data well (26% of purchases from 18% of spend). The reviews carousel and the plan to keep a control ad running are useful.
o2.biggest_mistake: Test spend is thin: about ₹4,500 per concept gives little to judge on. Broad targeting would blur the women-versus-men read it wants. The gate concept shows cabin dimensions that are not in the approved specs. It ignores the front-pocket request. Some copy leans on "quiet" and "smooth" as our own claims rather than review quotes.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add headlines and exact specs per format. Set a real test budget and audience split per concept. Keep quiet, smooth and sharp strictly as quoted review lines. Add a note on the front-pocket objection.

reason: Both pick the right three and keep the claims honest. Output 1 is closer to something I could hand to a team and launch, with scene timing, headlines, a sensible test budget and tighter claim rules. Output 2 reads a little more like our brand voice, but it is thinner on execution.
